analysis.title: Marketcolour + Flows / Eni/Sika/Norsk Hydro/ Siemens Energy
key_insights: US equities fell on the week: SPX -52bps to 7623 (8 of 11 sectors down, Consumer Staples -1.83%, Energy +2.51%, Tech +0.35%), NDX unchanged at 28957, RTY -29bps to 2775.
Signs of stabilization in the AI trade on Friday: semis/memory up (GS AI Semis basket +0.86%), while neoclouds kept struggling (Data Center basket -0.77%).
In Europe, EU Big Oils (+4.6%) was the dominant outperformer, UK Homebuilders (+1.2%) caught a bid as gilt yields stabilised, and Luxury (-4.8%) was the worst basket.

SPX 60-day realized volatility is about 10%, in the bottom quartile of the COVID and post-COVID era. The GS Momentum basket has moved more than 5%, more than in 2000, 2009 and 2020, with two months left in the year.
The GS floor saw about $20bn of net TMT selling over two weeks across all client types and execution channels, approaching the $23bn net sold over two weeks in the July AI selling episode.

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a third straight week (4 of the last 5), driven by long and short sales in single stocks, the largest de-grossing since late July. Industrials was among the most net sold sectors, at the fastest pace in 6+ months. Real Estate and Staples were the most net bought, pointing to a defensive posture.
Fundamental L/S managers are down 1.1% on the week (alpha -0.3%) and 3.8% MTD, giving back a quarter of their 2026 performance this month. They are still up 8.8% YTD, from +17.4% at end of June.

CTAs are long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile), nearly 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked. The S&P is below its short-term trend threshold, and the medium-term level is about 1.3% below Friday's close.
This week has FOMC and BOC on Wednesday, ECB Thursday and BOJ Friday, plus the heaviest Q3 earnings week (44% of S&P market cap reports; MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC Wednesday, AMZN, INTC Thursday).

GS maintains its forecast of one more ECB hike in December. A further hike in March is possible if energy prices keep rising, especially gas in a cold winter. GS sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes or a deposit rate above 3%.

Norsk Hydro cut to Neutral with a PT of NOK 79 from NOK 100 (10% upside). 2026/27 EBITDA is cut 6%/6% on lower earnings in Aluminium, Metal Markets and Energy and higher gas costs, and 2028 is raised 4% on cost revisions.
ENI Buy, PT EUR 29 (10% upside). EPS estimates rise 6.7%/11.0%/12.5% for 2026E/27E/28E on a lower tax rate and a higher dividend. It trades at a c.20% premium to EU Big Oils on 5.6x 2026E EV/DACF.

Sika Conviction List Buy, PT CHF 225 (25% upside). GS is 4% above consensus on 2028 EBITDA, rising to 7% if raw material costs revert to 2025 levels. The stock trades on c.23x P/E, about a 20% discount to its historical average.

Siemens Energy Conviction List Buy, PT EUR 212 (80% upside). The Capital Markets Day on Nov 11 is the next step in the re-rating. GS forecasts group EBITA up c.6x between FY2025 and FY2030, 11% ahead of Bloomberg consensus by FY2030, with shares on c.5x 2030E EV/EBITDA.

Hedge funds net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in over 5 months, on both short and long sales. Staples was the most net bought global sector, at the fastest pace in 10 weeks, from long buys and short covers.

EPS raised 6.7%/11.0%/12.5% for 2026E/27E/28E on a lower tax rate and higher dividend. The c.20% premium to EU Big Oils is seen as justified by the low-carbon satellite strategy, execution and exploration.

On the Conviction List. Upside from easing raw material and energy costs, with 2028 EBITDA 4% above consensus and 7% above if raw materials revert to 2025 levels. Trades on c.23x P/E, about a 20% discount to its history.
